Article.ArticleTitle: Microsurgical Clipping of a Giant Middle Cerebral Artery Aneurysm with Successful Postoperative Endovascular Mechanical Thrombectomy for Treatment of Emergent Large Vessel Occlusion.

Abstract.AbstractText: Giant intracranial aneurysms (>25mm) are uncommon. These lesions typically manifest clinically due to mass effect, acute hemorrhage, or thromboembolic events. To minimize the chances of poor clinical outcome, detailed operative planning and fully integrated considerations and collaboration among neurosurgical and endovascular techniques are essential prior to microsurgical clipping of ruptured giant aneurysms.

We describe a case involving a 15 year-old male with a ruptured giant middle cerebral artery aneurysm, treated with microsurgical clipping. After clip application, poor distal flow was demonstrated intraoperatively and emergent angiography demonstrated M1 occlusion with thrombus. A salvage procedure utilizing an endovascular mechanical thrombectomy reestablished distal flow resulting in a good neurological outcome.
To our knowledge, this is the first case report to describe microsurgical clipping of an aneurysm followed by successful postoperative endovascular mechanical thrombectomy.
